why: Record 0049 required the connection Cleanup inconsistency to be documented as a scoped existing finding rather than claimed as fixed. Record 0051 stated it was documented. That statement was ahead of the fact: it existed only as a sentence in the question payload, with no artefact behind it. This file is the artefact, written after the discrepancy was noticed.

findings.member: Cleanup(this IConnection connection, ushort replyCode, string message, CancellationToken)
findings.statement: The summary of this overload promises to close and dispose the connection 'without throwing any exceptions'. Only CloseAsync is inside the guard; DisposeAsync sits beside it and can throw, exactly as the channel overload did before this round corrected it.
findings.whyNotTouched: No measurement in this round attributes any observed failure to the connection overload. The channel overload was corrected because the trace put it on the failing path; this one has no such evidence, and record 0049 forbids widening the cause round without it.
findings.risk: The same class of defect as the channel overload: a failure while disposing a connection can replace the failure that caused the disposal. It would appear on connection teardown paths rather than on channel operations.
findings.recommendation: Handle it as its own small work item with its own evidence, not as a claimed side effect of this one.
